title: Mastering Crucial Conversations: The Power of Dialogue
coreMove: Diagnose whether the shared pool is filling or whether missing meaning is already shaping the outcome.
sourcePressure: Dialogue works by enlarging the Pool of Shared Meaning; silence shrinks the pool, decisions weaken, and later resistance often comes from meaning that never entered the room.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making dialogue sound like polite turn-taking instead of a decision-quality mechanism.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

hook: dictionary definition of a crucial conversation
tryThisNow: pick a conversation and journal about it without a chapter-specific test
examples: manager feedback in a conference room
spouse argument at the kitchen counter
student raising hand in a classroom
remote team silence as the only example shell

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: remote clinical-trial coordination call where rural site nurses stay silent about a recruitment barrier
exampleSpecs.audience: a trial coordinator responsible for patient enrollment across four clinics
exampleSpecs.stakes: the enrollment plan will fail because the sites withhold what patients are refusing to sign
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: three weeks after cheerful agreement, the coordinator compares zero enrollments with the call transcript and sees the pool had never included the nurses' real concerns
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A red zero sits in the enrollment dashboard beside three clinic names.

exampleSpecs.domain: community theater board choosing a season without hearing from the box-office volunteer
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer treasurer who thinks silence means broad approval
exampleSpecs.stakes: the board picks a play that loyal subscribers have been quietly warning against
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the treasurer notices the box-office volunteer keeps touching a folder of refund notes but never speaks, and asks what is not yet in the pool
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Wait," someone says, and a folder labeled refunds rests under the box-office volunteer's palm.

exampleSpecs.domain: factory maintenance shift handoff after a compressor repair
exampleSpecs.audience: a night-shift mechanic whose warning is missing from the day crew plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: a compressor restart could fail because the quietest person held back the odd vibration report
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor asks who has not put a fact into the pool, and the night mechanic taps the gauge log he had kept closed
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first signal is sensory before it is social: a pressure gauge logbook lies closed beside a dented thermos.

exampleSpecs.domain: food-truck permit hearing where neighborhood objections are polite but incomplete
exampleSpecs.audience: a city clerk trying to surface the actual concern before a vote
exampleSpecs.stakes: a permit decision may look fair while ignoring a loading-zone conflict everyone knows about
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the clerk hears repeated praise for entrepreneurship, notices nobody naming the blocked alley, and asks for the concern not yet said aloud
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You notice a laminated street map curls at the corner on a municipal table before anyone names the problem.

exampleSpecs.domain: museum exhibit label review with an outside historian on mute
exampleSpecs.audience: a curator leading a sensitive historical exhibit review
exampleSpecs.stakes: a label could publish with a serious omission because the invited historian feels ornamental
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the curator pauses when the historian unmutes twice and mutes again, then explicitly invites the missing source note into the shared meaning pool
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Only later does the miss become obvious: a sticky note reading source? clings to the glass of a display case.

exampleSpecs.domain: software incident review where customer support has the clearest pattern but lowest status
exampleSpecs.audience: an incident lead trying to reconstruct why a billing outage lasted eight hours
exampleSpecs.stakes: the fix targets the wrong service if support's ticket pattern stays outside the room
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before choosing a root cause, the lead asks support to pour in every complaint pattern, then predicts how the first answer changes when that data enters
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes when a support queue counter climbs past 300 on a wall monitor?

skillTargets: detect agreement that comes from withheld meaning
ask for missing facts, stories, feelings, and opinions by name
connect pool size to commitment after the meeting
notice when safety loss has made silence look like consent

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next group decision, write one sentence: The pool is missing _____. Ask one person who has been quiet to add that specific kind of meaning before the decision closes.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
